review_output: {"summary":"Both earlier MAJORs are fixed, and I found no concrete remaining regression in this scope. This is not a sign-off on the whole WP. (1) Lock order: materializeMetricRegistration reads the capture row without a lock, then locks Live, then FormSubmission, then Version (all FOR SHARE). That matches the stated Live -> FormSubmission -> Version order of the registration guard and the Live source trigger. A Live formId/videoId update now waits on the Live lock before its trigger can touch Version, so the deadlock cycle is gone. The regression test can tell the orders apart: it pauses on the first FOR SHARE query (the earlier capture read has no FOR SHARE, so the pause comes after the Live lock), confirms the updater is waiting on a lock, then requires the projection to return 'recorded' and the updater to fail only with its own deliberate rollback error. Under the old Version-first order, PostgreSQL's deadlock detector would abort one side, so one of those checks would fail. If the projection did not lock Live at all, the updater would not block and the 'blocked' check would fail. (2) Revoke: the migration revokes from PUBLIC, then loops over anon, authenticated and service_role and revokes table and function privileges. The test grants every privilege first, runs the real migration block, and checks that each role holds none of them. The multi-privilege has_table_privilege check returns true if any one is held, so 'false' means none are. has_function_privilege also counts PUBLIC grants, so the earlier PUBLIC revoke is covered indirectly. Only NIT-level test-robustness notes remain.","findings":[{"area":"lock-order regression test","file":"scripts/wp20-metric-persistence-disposable.mjs","severity":"NIT","confidence":0.7,"issue":"The 'blocked' check accepts any wait with wait_event_type='Lock'. It does not confirm that the updater is waiting on the Live row lock held by the projection.","evidence":"The polling loop only checks pg_stat_activity.wait_event_type === 'Lock'. The test still tells the orders apart through its outcome checks (projection 'recorded', updater error === rollback), so this is about clarity, not correctness.","impact":"If the test fails later, it is harder to tell which lock caused it. A future change in which the updater waits on an unrelated lock could still pass the 'blocked' check.","recommended_fix":"Optionally join pg_locks to pg_class and check that the waiting lock is on relation 'Live', or use pg_blocking_pids(updaterPid) to check that the blocker is the projection's backend.","required_test":"Assert that pg_blocking_pids(updaterPid) contains the projection's pg_backend_pid() and that the blocked lock's relation is \"Live\"."},{"area":"revoke regression test","file":"scripts/wp20-metric-persistence-disposable.mjs","severity":"NIT","confidence":0.75,"issue":"The test copies everything from 'DO $$ DECLARE api_role' to the end of the file and runs it. If any statement is added after the DO block later, it will be executed inside the test transaction.","evidence":"revokeBlock = migrationSql.slice(migrationSql.indexOf(\"DO $$ DECLARE api_role\")); the only check is startsWith.","impact":"The test could become brittle or have side effects if the migration is edited, though migrations are normally immutable once applied.","recommended_fix":"Stop the slice at the first 'END $$;' after the start, or assert that the copied block ends with 'END $$;' and has nothing after it.","required_test":"Assert that revokeBlock.trim().endsWith('END $$;') and that it contains exactly one DO block."}]}
